lines: Sample and hold that draws its samples from an internal simplex noise source rather than from a patched signal
A rising edge takes a new sample, and the number of channels here sets the number of channels at the output
Sets how fast the module travels through the noise, 1% to 100%, so how far apart in the noise two consecutive samples fall
0-10V scales the travel speed set by the speed knob, 0V freezing the travel and 10V giving the full knob speed
The value held since the last trigger, mapped into the voltage range picked on the menu
Menu — range sets the voltage span of the output, twelve presets from +/-10V to 0V-1V plus sliders for an arbitrary min and max; it starts at -1V to 1V
A 6HP blank panel carrying the alef's bits logo
Rotates the logo, 36 degrees per volt
Passes one randomly chosen channel of a polyphonic input, choosing again on each trigger
A rising edge chooses a new channel at random, which happens only while the poly input and the output are both patched
The polyphonic signal one channel of which reaches the output, 16 channels at most
The voltage of the chosen channel, on its own
Random noise generator whose values are held for an adjustable time, giving white noise at one end and stepped noise at the other
Sets how long each random value is held, 0 to 1ms, a new value being drawn every sample at zero
0-10V adds to the duration knob, 10V adding the full 1ms
The noise, -5V to 5V
Menu — random mode draws values evenly across the range (uniform) or clustered around the middle (gaussian), with a slider setting the gaussian deviation from 0.1 to 0.9
Eight step sequencer with a knob per step, a gate output per step, a randomize trigger and an end-of-cycle trigger
A rising edge advances to the next step
Sets how many steps play before the sequence returns to the first, 1 to 8
A rising edge sets all eight step knobs to new random values
Sets all eight step knobs to new random values
A rising edge returns the sequence to step 1, taking effect on the next clock pulse while the clock input is patched
A 1ms 10V trigger each time the sequence returns to its first step
The voltage of the knob for the current step, over the range picked on the menu, and 0V while the clock input is unpatched
Sets the voltage this step sends to the cv output, over the range picked on the menu
Carries 10V while the sequence is on this step and 0V otherwise
Menu — range sets the voltage span of the step knobs and the cv output, twelve presets from +/-10V to 0V-1V plus sliders for an arbitrary min and max
steps.notes: A step gate output above the number set by the steps knob is left at whatever it last held, since only the steps in play are refreshed.

lines: Clock divider with five outputs, each firing at a Fibonacci number of clock pulses
The clock being divided, each rising edge counting once
A rising edge restarts every division from zero
A 10V gate on every second clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every third clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every fifth clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every eighth clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every thirteenth clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
Clock divider with five outputs, each firing at a Lucas number of clock pulses
The clock being divided, each rising edge counting once
A rising edge restarts every division from zero
A 10V gate on every third clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every fourth clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every seventh clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every eleventh clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
A 10V gate on every eighteenth clock pulse, lasting as long as that pulse stays high
Multiplies a voltage and adds a whole number of volts to it, for fitting a signal into a chosen span of octaves
Multiplies the input by 0 to 2, in steps of 0.1
Adds a whole number of volts to the scaled signal, -3V to 3V, which moves a pitch signal by that many octaves
The voltage being scaled, 16 channels at most
The input multiplied by the scale knob with the offset knob added, clamped to -10V to 10V
octsclr.notes: The source and scaled jacks carry whatever you patch: a pitch voltage only tracks a volt per octave with the scale knob at 1.0, so neither jack is given a family.

lines: An eight stage shift register, each stage moving its value to the next on a trigger, with a probability control on every stage
The voltage shifted into the first stage, a fresh random voltage in the menu range being used at each trigger while this is unpatched
A rising edge shifts every stage along by one
Sets the chance that this stage stores the value shifted into it, 0 to 100%; below that chance the stage keeps its previous value and passes that one along
0-10V scales the storing chance set by the knob on that stage, 0V stopping the stage from storing anything
The voltage shifted into that stage at the last trigger
Menu — range sets the voltage span of the random voltages used while the in jack is unpatched, twelve presets from +/-10V to 0V-1V plus sliders for an arbitrary min and max
Menu — scrambled eggs! feeds every stage from a randomly chosen other stage instead of the stage before it
Two separate 1-to-5 multiples, each copying one polyphonic input to five outputs
The signal copied to the five outputs of that half
A copy of the input feeding that half, at that input's channel count
Six arithmetic combinations of two inputs, each result clamped to -10V to 10V
One of the two voltages being combined, taken as A in every operation
One of the two voltages being combined, taken as B in every operation
A plus B, clamped to -10V to 10V
A minus B, clamped to -10V to 10V
A multiplied by B, clamped to -10V to 10V
A divided by B, clamped to -10V to 10V
The remainder left after dividing A by B, clamped to -10V to 10V
The average of A and B, clamped to -10V to 10V
Six logic outputs comparing two inputs, each input counting as high above 0V
One of the two signals compared, taken as A, and counting as high above 0V
One of the two signals compared, taken as B, and counting as high above 0V
10V while both A and B are high, 0V otherwise
10V while either A or B is high, 0V otherwise
10V while exactly one of A and B is high, 0V otherwise
0V while both A and B are high, 10V otherwise
0V while either A or B is high, 10V otherwise
0V while exactly one of A and B is high, 10V otherwise
Mutes and unmutes a signal on each trigger, the chance of muting set by a knob
The signal that is passed or silenced, 16 channels at most
A rising edge draws again on the probability, either muting the signal or letting it through
Sets the chance of muting at each trigger, 0 to 100%
Adds to the prob knob, 10V adding the full 100%
The input signal, either passed through or silenced
Menu — fade in/out replaces the instant mute with a fade, a slider setting the fade length from 5ms to 10 seconds
Sample player that starts the sample again on a new polyphonic channel at each trigger, so repeats overlap
Sets how many channels are cycled through, 1 to 16
Starts the sample on the next channel
A rising edge starts the sample on the next channel
How far that channel has played through the sample, over the range picked on the menu
The left channel of the sample, or a mix of all its channels while the right output is unpatched
The right channel of the sample, or a copy of the left one for a mono sample
Menu — load sample opens a file dialog, and the loaded file is named below it; clicking that name unloads it
Menu — gain multiplies the sample playback by 1 to 2
Menu — phase range sets the voltage span of the phase output, twelve presets from +/-10V to 0V-1V plus sliders for an arbitrary min and max
Eight inputs with a lamp each, for showing which gates in a patch are high
The lamp beside this jack brightens with the voltage here and is full at 10V, or toggles on each rising edge in latch mode
Menu — latch makes a rising edge toggle a lamp on or off, in place of a lamp following the voltage
lights.notes: The README says a lamp stays on while its input is above 5V; the installed code instead sets lamp brightness to the input voltage divided by 10, which is what the line describes.

lines: A 64 step sequencer of randomly generated voltages, quantized to a root and scale, with random per-cycle offsets called slips and a second modulation sequence
A rising edge advances one step
Sets the root note the sequence is quantized to, C through B
0-10V sweeps the root across the twelve notes, or reads a pitch voltage with root input v/oct switched on in the menu
Sets how many steps play before the sequence returns to its starting step, 1 to 64
0-10V sets the number of steps over the whole 1 to 64 span, in place of the steps knob
A rising edge returns the sequence to its starting step
Picks the scale the sequence is quantized to: chromatic, major, minor, major pentatonic, minor pentatonic, dorian, lydian, mixolydian, phrygian, locrian or blues
0-10V steps through the eleven scales, in place of the scale knob
Sets the step the sequence starts and restarts from, 1 to 64
0-10V sets the starting step over the whole 1 to 64 span, in place of the start knob
Draws a new random sequence of 64 values
A rising edge draws a new random sequence of 64 values
A 100ms 10V trigger each time the sequence returns to its starting step
Sets the chance that a step reaches the outputs, 0 to 100%; a skipped step repeats the last voltage and puts out no gate
0-10V sets the step chance over the whole 0 to 100% span, in place of the prob knob
A rising edge draws a new random modulation sequence
Draws a new random modulation sequence
Sets what share of the 64 steps are given a random offset, 0 to 100%, a fresh set of steps being chosen at the start of each cycle
0-10V sets the share of offset steps over the whole 0 to 100% span, in place of the slips knob
The quantized voltage of the current step, with that step's random offset added where it has one
Carries the clock voltage while a step plays, and 0V while a step is skipped
Carries the clock voltage while a step that has a random offset plays, and 0V otherwise
The voltage of the current step of the modulation sequence, over the range picked on the menu
Menu — root input v/oct makes the root cv jack read a pitch voltage, the twelve semitones of each volt picking the root, in place of a 0-10V sweep
Menu — poly channels sets how many channels the sequence and gate outputs carry, each clock pulse moving to the next channel
Menu — poly mod output carries the modulation sequence on the same channels as the main sequence; switched off it is monophonic
Menu — remap on generate fits the random values to their ranges when a sequence is generated; switched off, the fitting happens at playback, so a range change reshapes the existing sequence
Menu — sequence range, slip sequence range and mod sequence range each set a voltage span, twelve presets from +/-10V to 0V-1V plus sliders for an arbitrary min and max
Menu — mod sequence options quantize the modulation sequence to the same root and scale, add the slip offsets to it, and apply the step chance to it
Menu — add slipspander places a slipspander expander to the right, whose lit note buttons then replace the scale knob
slips.notes: Input 8 (quantize) and output 0 (quantize) are configured in the code but placed on no panel position, so they have no line and no family.

lines: Expander for slips, placed immediately to its right, whose twelve note buttons set a custom scale for slips to quantize to
Puts that note into the custom scale while it is lit
Note — with no note lit, slips quantizes to the scale picked by its own scale knob
Generates a trigger when an input signal turns around, crosses a threshold, or both, with a scope drawing the signal and its triggers
The signal the triggers are taken from, 16 channels at most, each channel having its own scope tab
Sets the threshold crossed in through zero mode, -10V to 10V
Scales the threshold set by the zero knob, 10V giving the full knob value and negative voltages flipping its sign
Picks what makes a trigger: direction, where the signal turns from rising to falling or back; through zero, where it crosses the threshold; or both of those
Sets the chance that a trigger is generated when the condition is met, 0 to 100%
0-10V scales the chance set by the prob knob, 10V giving the full knob value
A 1ms 10V trigger at each crossing, or in latch mode a gate that flips between 0V and 10V at each crossing
Menu — trigger mode picks a 1ms trigger at each crossing, or a latch that flips the output between 0V and 10V
Menu — freeze when idle holds the scope drawing in place while the source jack is unpatched, in place of clearing it
Menu — scope mode draws the active channel's tab centred on 0V (bipolar) or from 0V upwards (unipolar)
Menu — time scale sets how much signal the active channel's tab holds, 64, 256 or 2048 samples
Oscillator that reads its waveform from a table of random noise, refilled on demand from one of three noise sources
Sets the frequency, 32.7Hz to 1046.5Hz
Shifts the frequency set by the freq knob a volt per octave, the voltage clamped to -4V to 4V
A rising edge refills the wavetable with fresh noise
Refills the wavetable with fresh noise
The oscillator, -5V to 5V
Menu — table size sets the length of the wavetable, 64 to 1024 samples, which takes effect at the next refill
Menu — mode picks the noise the table is filled from: rand for independent random values, simplex for a smooth noise curve, worley for a cellular one
Menu — noise increment sets how far apart the table's samples are taken in the simplex and worley noise, 0.01 to 0.1, so how jagged the wave is
Re-orders the channels of a polyphonic signal on a trigger, by shuffling them or rotating them one place
The polyphonic signal whose channels are re-ordered, and whose channel count the output takes
A rising edge re-orders the channels by the mode picked on the menu
A rising edge puts the channels back into the order they arrive in
The input's channels in their current order
Menu — mode picks what a trigger does: shuffle the channels at random, rotate them up one place, or rotate them down one place
Counts in volts between two limits on each trigger, with a separate count for every channel of the trigger input
A rising edge adds the inc value to the count for that channel
A rising edge returns the count to the start value; a monophonic signal here resets every channel, a polyphonic one resets only the matching channel
Sets the voltage the count begins from and wraps back to, -10V to 10V
Sets the voltage the count wraps at, -10V to 10V
Sets how much is added at each trigger, -10V to 10V, a negative value counting downwards
The current count for that channel, wrapping round between the start and end values
polycounter.notes: Start and end are swapped internally when start is the higher of the two, so the count always runs between them.
